name: affinity-point-sized-nameplate
exporter: Affinity Designer 2.4 - File > Export > SVG, from a document started on a print preset
story: A name plate drawn in a print-unit document, so the page is stated in points: 960pt x 540pt, which is exactly 1280 x 720 CSS pixels.
idioms: width="960pt" height="540pt" with viewBox="0 0 960 540" - the physical unit on width/height only, and the viewBox in bare user units
the root style preamble Affinity always writes: fill-rule:evenodd;clip-rule:evenodd;stroke-linejoin:round;stroke-miterlimit:2;
xmlns:serif="http://www.serif.com/" with serif:id carrying the original layer name beside a hyphenated id (id="Name-plate" serif:id="Name plate")
colours as rgb() inside inline style strings, plus fill-opacity rather than opacity
px-suffixed x/y attributes on <text> even though the page is in points
PostScript-name-first font stacks with the plain family second: font-family:'Archivo-Bold', 'Archivo', and font-weight repeated numerically alongside
standalone="no" in the XML declaration, 4-space indentation
whyThisMatters: This is the millimetre finding in a second unit, and it exists so the answer cannot be a millimetre special case: a conversion that hardcodes mm reads this page at 960 x 540 and places a full-page design as a two-thirds-size object, which looks like a design decision rather than a bug. Points are not exotic here either - Affinity and every other print-first tool default to them, and a university design department is a print department. It also carries the second Affinity export in the corpus, so serif:id and the rgb()-in-style habit are pinned by more than one file.
